# Codex compatibility adapter

This is a local adapter, not official Codex support. Upstream files are unchanged at cursor/plugins commit ae5650febf4320793844c12c4adaa937f417f8da (pstack 0.15.36).

Read the requested upstream SKILL.md in full and its relevant leaf skills/playbook before working. Resolve upstream relative paths against the upstream file, not the wrapper. Bundled skill names refer to pstack/skills/<name>/SKILL.md here; deslop, control-cli and control-ui refer to cursor-team-kit/skills/<name>/SKILL.md. Do not resolve bare tdd to the pre-existing unrelated Codex skill. Discoverable names are poteto-mode and pstack-<upstream-name> for every other skill.

System/developer instructions, user scope, repository AGENTS.md and REVIEW.md, and existing authority boundaries take precedence over upstream defaults. Installation does not authorize messaging others, deploying, purchasing, changing credentials, merging, force-pushing, deleting data, or activating external bots/services. Preserve repository-specific comment, artifact, test and UI rules. Skill defect edits stay separate from the user's task.

Map read/search/shell and todo operations to available Codex tools. Cursor Task types, model slugs, rules paths, custom-mode UI, /loop, Bugbot, automations, Origin, transcript search and Cursor built-in create-skill are not installed capabilities. Use the existing Codex skill-creator for skill authoring. Do not run setup-pstack to write Cursor configuration. No bundled scripts, setup steps, dependency installers, bots or binaries have been executed or runtime-certified; inspect a needed script and its dependencies before authorized use.

For authorized delegation use available Codex collaboration tools with fresh isolated contexts and output locations. Read the relevant upstream agent definition and pass its required grounding explicitly; native Cursor agent registration is unavailable. Inherit the current Codex model; do not invoke external model services or pretend Grok/Claude are available. For an arena/interrogate panel use two independent same-model reviewers when supported, explicitly report loss of model diversity, and retain the arena verification steps. If delegation is unavailable or disallowed, report the missing independent panel and perform only a clearly labeled single-agent pass; never call that a complete independent review or passing merge gate. Other required unavailable features remain explicit gaps, not simulated success.

For Tomato review use interrogate (via pstack-interrogate) and its arena, in-your-own-words and principle dependencies. It reports verified findings and does not apply fixes. Re-run each reported command against the exact reviewed head, deduplicate root causes, report dropped findings and coverage gaps; static concerns that cannot be run remain separately labeled unverified risks and cannot become a false all-clear. Repository verification and merge requirements still apply. Fixes belong to the separately authorized fix phase and invalidate the prior review. The old code-review skill remains installed, but is no longer Tomato's mandatory or unique review entry.
